card.name: Mid-sentence words in technical web prose
card.fires_on: Ordinary connecting words such as 'a', 'support', 'for' or 'indirectly' in the middle of a sentence in technical or general web prose. Seen most in patent-style hardware descriptions and search-engine text, with no single word class.

modes.label: Patent-style hardware text
modes.description: Verbs and prepositions inside descriptions of PCI buses and adapters.
modes.example: Typical PCI bus implementations will<< support>> four PCI

modes.label: The word 'a' before a noun phrase
modes.description: The article 'a' after a verb or linking word, before a descriptive noun.
modes.example: By 2007, search engines had incorporated<< a>> wide range of undisclosed factors in their ranking

modes.label: Disclaimer and course wording
modes.description: Adverbs or articles inside notices and course descriptions.
modes.example: It is neither intended nor implied to be<< a>> substitute for professional medical advice.
